selectedFunctions.label: NodeDAO Claim matured native ETH withdrawals
warnings: Static deployment-bound source/ABI metadata only; no persistent runtime identity, backing, funding, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or complete-workflow assurance. Exact grants, independent policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value checks still apply. stakeETH alone is payable; its msg.value is the native ETH deposit. All selected exit methods are nonpayable and require zero native value.

Ethereum NodeDAO nETH pool proxy 0xf3C79408164abFB6fD5dDfE33B084E4ad2C07c18 currently resolves to NethPool implementation 0x9c6F151fF54B9820d4C54335369b76729e6503FA in verifier proxyResolution, implementation() and EIP1967 slot at block 0x190a577. This is current binding, not an initial implementation assumption or permanent attestation; owner can upgrade and DAO can pause/change configuration.

stakeETH() accepts ONLY native ETH, minimum 0.01 ETH enforced by current source, NOT the 0.000001 ETH/no-minimum claims in older docs. It retains msg.value in the fixed pool, calculates floor-rounded shares, updates accounting and mints nETH only to msg.sender through fixed token 0xc6572019548dfeba782ba5a2093c836626c7789a. No ERC20 deposit, referral, arbitrary recipient, permit or signature authorization exists in this method.

The nETH token whiteListMint/whiteListBurn names restrict the CALLING pool, not end-user allowlisting: current token liquidStakingContractAddress equals the admitted pool. Exits burn only msg.sender's existing nETH without allowance or third-party owner authority; source does not check historic deposits. Docs nevertheless tell users to unstake only after previously staking through NodeDAO; do not promise app acceptance of externally acquired nETH or broader legal/KYC/jurisdiction eligibility.

unstakeETH(uint256) is an immediate attempt: it converts caller nETH shares to floor-rounded native ETH, gathers configured execution/consensus-vault funds if needed, burns caller shares, then sends ETH only to caller with empty calldata. Insufficient funds or a rejecting recipient contract reverts. It does not automatically create a delayed withdrawal; no liquidity/timing promise.

requestWithdrawals(uint256) is the distinct asynchronous path and reverts CanUnstakeETH if the pool's own ETH balance already covers the requested payout. It burns caller nETH immediately, reduces accounting, and records fixed claimAmount and request block under caller; queued claims no longer accrue staking yield. It checks raw pool balance rather than the immediate exit's aggregate vault-funding logic. No FIFO priority or complete reservation of all earlier queue obligations is promised.

claimWithdrawals(receiver,requestIds) is permissionless settlement of requests OWNED BY receiver; receiver is both queue key and fixed payout recipient, not a way to redirect someone else's claims. All IDs must exist, have nonzero stored withdrawalAmount, be unclaimed and mature; repeated/already claimed IDs revert the batch. State marks all selected requests claimed before funds gathering and empty-calldata native ETH payout, with atomic revert on failure.

Observed withdrawalDelayBlocks is 36000, not a guaranteed 7-day duration; source initializes 50400 and governance may set up to 72000 blocks. Maturity uses current delay at claim time, so governance changes affect already queued claims. Delay is a minimum block eligibility test, not a payout deadline; vault liquidity, pauses and recipient behavior can still prevent settlement. Request storage narrows withdrawalAmount/claimAmount to uint128 and exchange to uint96; ordinary quantities must fit those source bounds.

Exchange accounting is NOT a live reserve/backing price: Rate.sol accrues estimated yield from mutable rate-manager APR and block count, only when underlying accounting is at least 32 ETH, with integer rounding and first-deposit 1:1 fallback. No minimum output, maximum input or deadline is encoded by selected methods; no explicit direct stake/exit fee, but execution-layer rewards are reduced by mutable PoolConfig DAO commission and DAO strategy/validator management affect funds.

Current dependencies: nETH token is nonproxy; ELVault proxy 0xa9d21395a58d832d2c44605D286560876DdEe8f3 implementation 0x3dd8D9074F2a2656144125a3dD04AbCE01AFaC23; consensus vault proxy 0x4b8dc35b44296d8d6dcc7afebbbe283c997e80ae implementation 0x1BeFbaD5c77b46DE397CFD4472f77E0Dbc566Ce3. Fixed calls can reinvest rewards; dynamic user targets/selectors/bytes are not exposed. Dependency upgrades/settings and mutable commission remain limitations, not isolation claims. Direct vault methods, strategy/reward donations, rnETH/restaking, validator, arbitrary upgrade/admin and callback surfaces are excluded.

claimWithdrawals(receiver,requestIds) is permissionless settlement of requests OWNED BY receiver; receiver is both queue key and fixed payout recipient, not a way to redirect someone else's claims. All IDs must exist, have nonzero stored withdrawalAmount, be unclaimed and mature; repeated/already claimed IDs revert the batch. State marks all selected requests claimed before funds gathering and empty-calldata native ETH payout, with atomic revert on failure.

devdoc.details: This contract implements an upgradeable proxy. It is upgradeable because calls are delegated to an implementation address that can be changed. This address is stored in storage in the location specified by https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967[EIP1967], so that it doesn't conflict with the storage layout of the implementation behind the proxy.

constructor.details: Initializes the upgradeable proxy with an initial implementation specified by `_logic`. If `_data` is nonempty, it's used as data in a delegate call to `_logic`. owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

proxiableUUID().details: Implementation of the ERC1822 {proxiableUUID} function. This returns the storage slot used by the implementation. It is used to validate the implementation's compatibility when performing an upgrade. IMPORTANT: A proxy pointing at a proxiable contract should not be considered proxiable itself, because this risks bricking a proxy that upgrades to it, by delegating to itself until out of gas. Thus it is critical that this function revert if invoked through a proxy. This is guaranteed by the `notDelegated` modifier.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the value {ERC20} uses, unless this function is overridden; NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

increaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically increases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

# nETH

Tokenized ETH staking pool to maximize returns for stakers

A tokenized ETH staking pool designed to provide the highest possible returns to stakers The purpose of the NodeDAO staking pool is to give ETH holders the opportunity to maximize staking returns by participating in the Ethereum 2.0 consensus process and allow them to use their stake to harvest additional returns in various DeFi protocols with the help of the NodeDAO token nETH.

## Introduction:

 The DeFi world is constantly evolving, providing exciting opportunities to maximize returns on your cryptocurrency holdings.

NodeDAO's nETH, a liquidity staking token based on Ethereum POS consensus. nETH enables you to earn additional rewards through your staked ETH while contributing to th**e security of the Ethereum network and other networks**.

## Introduction to the staking pool

The liquidity staking pool takes your DeFi experience to the next level. By leveraging the smooth exchange mechanism between nETH and ETH, giving nETH liquidity value, allowing users to obtain more benefits through the Defi scenarios that NodeDAO is looking for for users.

## How does it work?

1. **Stake your ETH into NodeDAO's** staking pool and **get nETH in return.**
2. **NodeDAO is responsible** for staking ETH in the staking pool as a validator, obtaining native POS staking income, and distributing income to users through the growth of nETH's exchange rate.

## Benefits of nETH

* The **power of compound interest:** Increase your rewards in a compounded manner by earning interest from your initial stake and re-staking pool rewards.
* **Flexibility:** Keep control of your staked ETH. You can easily withdraw your ETH tokens from the re-staking pool at any time.

## Conclusion:

**Don't let your staked ETH sit idle**. Get more benefits on top of Ethereum POS rewards.

Submit a withdrawal request Select the "Unstake" tab, choose the option to withdraw nETH, and specify the desired amount. Remember that you will not be able to exchange or unstake nETH unless you have previously staked ETH through the NodeDAO platform. ### Step **3.** Confirm the transaction. Please check your wallet balance, nETH will be unstaked and burned. If the redemption pool has enough funds, ETH will be sent to your wallet immediately; if the redemption pool does not have enough funds, unstaking will perform an asynchronous withdrawal process, and you can claim the withdrawn ETH for up to 7 days. The withdrawal process for rnETH is the same.

Unlike other rebasing tokens, nETH does not rebase, the number of tokens in your wallet will remain the same. The value of nETH will appreciate over time as it generates staking rewards. Our protocol is designed so that the nETH price always rises in ETH terms to reflect your staking returns. This makes nETH a valuable asset that can be used directly as collateral in DeFi applications without wrapping. Step 2 - Choose your preferred walletBy staking with us, you can earn rewards while watching your nETH tokens appreciate relative to ETH as long as our node operators continue to generate staking rewards. Start staking with us today and earn rewards! ### Step 1 - Go to [NodeDAO's website](https://app.nodedao.com) ### Step 2 - Choose your preferred wallet Click on "Connect Wallet" and select your preferred wallet. Once connected you will be able to see your ETH balance ### Step 3 - Start Staking Enter the amount of ETH you want to stake and click on "Stake". ### Step 4- Confirm the transaction in your wallet Review the transaction details and press Confirm. Done. ### Step 5 - Now you will have nETH in your wallet Voila! You will see a new **token in your wallet called nETH** which represents your staked ETH and **grows with the daily staking rewards.**

#### What staking options are available in NodeDAO?

### NodeDAO Pool

#### How does the NodeDAO Pool work?

Through its Pool product, NodeDAO operates a network of validators. For every set of 32 ETH deposited by a user, NodeDAO will build a new validator and integrate it into the network. The rewards generated by these validators are distributed to users in proportion to their ETH contribution to the pool.

#### What is the minimum staking amount?

There is no minimum amount required.

#### How do I track my staking reward amounts in the NodeDAO pool?

You can track them from the various operators' platforms.

#### How do I withdraw my deposits and rewards from the NodeDAO pool?

Pre-Shanghai, stakers will find nETH liquidity on the open market. The price of nETH will be determined by stakers' demand to buy nETH against the open market price and yield, and by operators who may take advantage of arbitrage opportunities to reduce their stake in the liquidity pool.

After the Shanghai upgrade, NodeDAO users will be able to redeem their nETH tokens for ETH directly within the platform at a rate proportional to the ETH and nETH supply.

#### Is NodeDAO non-custodial?

Funds are locked in the Ethereum network, and withdrawals are implemented by the liquidstaking contract managed by the DAO.

#### Do I get nETH rewards by staking in NodeDAO?

With NodeDAO, staking your ETH will always earn rewards, which will be recorded on the beacon chain. Our tokens serve as proof of your ETH deposit and accumulated rewards, allowing you to trade, earn more returns, and even use them as collateral for borrowing.

#### What happens if I transfer/swap my nETH tokens?

When you swap or transfer nETH tokens that represent your rewards in the NodeDAO pool, you are actually transferring your principal and rewards to someone else.
